transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-03
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Stratus), Tom Higgins (Stratus), Diego Martins (Stratus)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Stratus is exploring hosted embeddings + reranker flow for their internal search product. Primary asks: cost at scale, latency for reranker on top of k-NN retrieval, security/SOC2, and ability to run pilot and compare to Pinecone/Elastic stack. Demo covered Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint, search+rerank pattern (retrieve then model-based rerank), Console walk-through of Optimize suggestions, and a quick benchmark demo on sample dataset. Next steps: pricing calc, security docs, pilot kickoff.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint; vector index patterns; rerank endpoint and token costs; candidate set sizing (top_k); batching & latency tradeoffs; Console Optimize recommendations; SOC2/compliance questions; pilot plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, AE on this account. We've got about 50 minutes, we'll walk through hosted embeddings + reranking patterns and leave time for Qs. Liam, wanna intro?
[00:22] Liam Patel: Yeah hey, I'm Liam, solutions engineer. I'll show a quick demo of the API and Console, and then a short live runner showing rerank latencies on a sample set. Quick note: transcript auto captions may mangle some acronyms.
[00:35] Anika Rao: Thanks, we mainly want to see how the hosted path will fit our platform. We're currently on Elastic + a custom BERT reranker, thinking about replacing parts with a vector store. Main concerns: latency under 100ms median, and cost per query at ~500k qpm monthly.
[01:02] Tom Higgins: Also curious about PCI/PII handling and audit logs. We run in AWS with cross-account VPC peering.
[01:14] Diego Martins: From ML side I'll focus on quality: do we do retrieval-then-rerank? how many candidates are sensible, and how much does rerank add to latency & cost.
[01:35] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: 1) API overview (embeddings + rerank endpoints), 2) Console Optimize tips, 3) live-ish runner and numbers, 4) security/compliance Qs, 5) next steps.
[02:03] Liam Patel: Jumping in — embeddings endpoint is a simple REST call, returns vector arrays. Typical dimensionality examples: 768/1024/1536 in our model catalog, and we return floats as part of payload. Example call shown in Console or SDKs.
[02:28] Anika Rao: Do we host the vector index or do we expect customers to bring their own store?
[02:35] Liam Patel: For hosted API we provide both options — you can use Redwood's managed index (we support approximate neighbors with HNSW under the hood) or export vectors to your own store like Pinecone/Weaviate or even Elastic dense vec. Managed index simplifies latency/cost tuning because we operate the index alongside inference.
[02:58] Diego Martins: Curious about refresh rates. Our dataset updates hourly.
[03:06] Liam Patel: That's fine, we support incremental inserts and TTLs. If you have a high write QPS we can talk Dedicated capacity.
[03:18] Tom Higgins: Security quick: where do logs and vectors live? Are embeddings stored encrypted?
[03:25] Maya Chen: Hosted vectors are encrypted at rest, keys managed with KMS. We can also configure retention policies or opt out of storing vectors. We include audit trails in the Console with token-level tracing. We'll send the SOC2 whitepaper after.
[03:47] Anika Rao: Good. Show us the actual retrieval + rerank pattern please.
[03:55] Liam Patel: Sure — typical pattern: 1) embeddings(endpoint.embed) for query -> d vector, 2) k-NN retrieve top_k candidates from the vector index (we demo with top_k=100), 3) call rerank endpoint (model-based) to score candidates with context and produce final ordering. We also support two-stage scoring where the model produces a relevance score or a delta to boost ranking.
[04:30] [screen share noise] Liam Patel: (shows Console) Here's a sample dataset — product docs. Console has an 'Optimize' tab that suggests top_k and quantization profiles based on your query distribution. See this suggested top_k of 75 for median query length of 12 tokens.
[04:56] Diego Martins: How does Optimize derive cost estimates?
[05:03] Liam Patel: It takes your actual token distribution and recommends batching, caching, and top_k. It then simulates per-request token counts and computes per 1M requests cost given model and quantization. It's heuristic but generally close to reality.
[05:24] Anika Rao: Let's see the reranker call shape.
[05:29] Liam Patel: Example payload: { query: "...", candidates: [{id: x, text: "..."},...], context: {...}} — we stream back scores. Important to note: reranker is charged as model calls (per-token + per-response). So reranking 100 candidates with a 512-token context will have nontrivial cost. That's why candidates size matters, and Optimize helps tune that.
[06:05] Tom Higgins: Can rerank be done in a batch—like we pass multiple queries at once to amortize overhead?
[06:12] Liam Patel: Yes, our API supports batch rerank calls. However batching increases latency tail if you wait to accumulate requests. For batch sizes > 8 you'll see better throughput/cost but worse p95 latency. It's a classic tradeoff.
[06:31] Maya Chen: For Stratus use-case — medium latency requirement 100ms median — we'd suggest keeping rerank top_k around 10-20 for strict latency, prefilter aggressively with fast lexical filters, and use small reranker model variants.
[06:50] Diego Martins: What are model variants? Like quantized versions?
[06:55] Liam Patel: Exactly — smaller-sized reranker models, or quantized variants (int8/4) that reduce compute and cost. Also you can pick a lighter model arch for reranking. Optimize will recommend which to try first based on evals.
[07:12] Anika Rao: Can you show cost math for 100k queries vs 500k?
[07:18] Maya Chen: Quick example in Console: embeddings call is $0.0002 per embed (example), rerank call depends on tokens — say $0.001 per rerank on average. For 500k queries with top_k=10 we estimate X — we'll send detailed calc after this call.
[07:40] Tom Higgins: Please do. Also show us how to integrate with our VPC.
[07:45] Liam Patel: Hosted API uses TLS; for Private we offer VPC connector and on-prem. Hosted can be used with IP allowlists and SSO for Console. If you need dedicated connectivity we map out a VPC peering private control plane for Private deployments.
[08:08] Diego Martins: Demo run?
[08:12] Liam Patel: I'll run a small live benchmark. Using a 2k doc corpus, retrieval top_k=50 then rerank top_k=10. I'll log median & p95.
[08:25] [typing noises]
[08:40] Liam Patel: Running now... retrieval median 12ms, reranker median 78ms, end-to-end median 105ms, p95 210ms. Note: this is a small test in hosted environment, not tuned for your traffic.
[09:05] Anika Rao: 105ms median is close to our 100ms target. Can you reduce to sub-100?
[09:12] Liam Patel: With smaller top_k and lighter reranker model, yes — if we push top_k to 20 and use the int8 variant we get median ~82ms in this demo run. Also prefix/KV caching helps if queries repeat.
[09:35] Diego Martins: What does KV cache mean here?
[09:38] Liam Patel: It's our prefix caching — if your reranker uses repeated shared context (like product metadata), we cache those internal activations to avoid recomputation. It helps amortize cost for repeated prompt contexts.
[09:54] Tom Higgins: Any data residency controls?
[09:58] Maya Chen: We have region controls – you can pin models and storage to regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[10:12] Anika Rao: Security: where is audit data surfaced?
[10:16] Liam Patel: Console has per-request logs with redaction options. We can integrate to your SIEM via log streams.
[10:25] [brief silence]
[10:30] Diego Martins: On indexing: you said HNSW. Is there a way to run brute-force exact search for small sets?
[10:37] Liam Patel: Yes. For small corpora we fallback to exact linear scan. And we expose control flags.
[10:44] Anika Rao: Are embeddings reversible? We worry about PII leak.
[10:49] Maya Chen: Embeddings are high-dimensional floats and not invertible in practice. We also support token-level suppression and can avoid storing vectors. We'll provide more detailed threat modeling in the security doc.
[11:05] Tom Higgins: Ok. Could you walk through the SDK flow?
[11:09] Liam Patel: Sure — node/python snippets in the Console. Example: const vec = await client.embeddings.create({model: 'redwood-embed-1024', input: 'query'}); then client.search.query({vector: vec.data, top_k: 50}). Then client.rerank.score({query: '...', candidates: [...]}) — pretty straightforward.
[11:36] Diego Martins: How are we billed? per-embed + per-rerank? Is there a fixed index cost?
[11:43] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based: per-embed, per-token for rerank, and optional storage for large index sizes. For Dedicated there's a reserved capacity commit.
[11:55] Anika Rao: If we do 500k qpm monthly — that's a lot, I think we mean monthly queries 500k (not qps).
[12:02] Maya Chen: Right, monthly. We'll model a few scenarios in the TCO sheet.
[12:09] Liam Patel: Also note network egress costs if you export vectors regularly.
[12:15] [short chuckle]
[12:18] Anika Rao: Can we use your rerank endpoint to return structured outputs like classification or labels?
[12:24] Liam Patel: Yes, the model can return structured JSON or a score. We support function-calling-ish patterns and structured output parsing. For rerank you'd typically return a numeric relevance and optional reason string.
[12:40] Tom Higgins: Do you support streaming rerank responses?
[12:44] Liam Patel: Streaming is supported for generation calls; for rerank we stream partial scoring if the model emits incremental tokens, but usually rerank is synchronous since scores are numeric and small.
[13:00] Diego Martins: In the demo run, are you running on shared hosted capacity?
[13:05] Liam Patel: Yes, this was on hosted. For strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated.
[13:12] Anika Rao: Could Dedicated help with p95 reduction?
[13:15] Maya Chen: Yes — Dedicated gives pinned GPU pools which lower contention and improve p95. We also offer autoscaling policies to manage bursts.
[13:30] [screen share: Console Optimize tab]
[13:35] Liam Patel: Optimize suggestions here — it recommended quantization of reranker model to int8 and moving to top_k=20. It also flagged a caching opportunity for frequent query prefixes.
[13:50] Diego Martins: How do you measure quality regression when we change models or quantize?
[13:55] Liam Patel: We run evals against your labeled prompt set in the Console. You can provide a golden set; Optimize will score candidate configurations and show precision/recall differences. Also regression alerts can be tied to production prompt samples.
[14:16] Anika Rao: If we want to pilot, can you simulate our traffic?
[14:21] Maya Chen: Yes — for pilot we ingest a sample of your logs and run a pilot run with cost & latency estimates. We'll do a one-week pilot with 100k queries/day synthetic mix to validate.
[14:36] Tom Higgins: For pilot networking, will we need a VPN?
[14:41] Liam Patel: Typically not for hosted; we can use API keys and IP allowlist. For Private or Dedicated we can use VPC peering.
[14:55] Diego Martins: Are there any pre-built connectors for message buses?
[14:59] Liam Patel: We have ingestion connectors and pub/sub hooks — we'll share docs.
[15:08] Anika Rao: You mentioned re-ranking cost is token-based — what's a typical token count per candidate?
[15:15] Liam Patel: If you send candidate text only a few tokens each maybe 20-50 tokens; if you include product context then maybe 200 tokens per candidate. A clever approach is to send minimal candidate text and include a short context.
[15:32] Diego Martins: So for 10 candidates at 50 tokens each + query 20 tokens we have ~520 tokens => rerank cost accordingly.
[15:41] Liam Patel: Exactly. So batching candidates into a single model call is often cheaper than N separate calls.
[15:49] [murmur] Anika Rao: Are there recommended eval metrics for e-commerce relevance?
[15:54] Liam Patel: Precision@k, MRR, and NDCG are typical. Optimize reports these.
[16:05] Tom Higgins: Any limitations on candidate size?
[16:08] Liam Patel: Candidate list size has practical limits based on prompt length. We recommend keeping per-request token count under model context windows — we support long context models for huge lists but cost scales.
[16:25] Diego Martins: For our internal metrics here's our profile: average query length 8 tokens, 60% repeat queries, peak 200 qps — Diego later to share full.
[16:35] Maya Chen: That's helpful — Diego, if you share that profile we'll run targeted TCO scenarios.
[16:42] Diego Martins: Will do.
[16:46] Anika Rao: One more question: how do you handle relevance explainability?
[16:51] Liam Patel: Reranker can return reasons, but explainability is limited — we provide per-candidate highlights and delta scores. For deeper explainability we'd recommend a hybrid approach with feature-based signals.
[17:08] Tom Higgins: How do you handle model rollouts? We prefer canary first.
[17:12] Maya Chen: Console supports canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback to older model if quality drops. You can pin versioned models.
[17:23] Anika Rao: Demo done — can we discuss pricing specifics?
[17:28] Maya Chen: High-level now: embeddings per call, rerank per-token. For 500k monthly queries we modeled three configs: heavy (top_k=50), medium (top_k=20), light (top_k=10). We'll share the spreadsheet.
[17:45] Diego Martins: For evaluation, how quickly can we get our labeled set into Console for automatic scoring?
[17:50] Liam Patel: Usually within a day if you provide it as CSV. We'll help with a template.
[17:58] Anika Rao: Ok, security again — you said we can opt out of storing vectors. If we opt out, does retrieval still work?
[18:05] Liam Patel: If you don't store vectors you need to host your own store or re-embed on the fly. Retrieval without stored vectors implies extra latency and cost.
[18:18] Tom Higgins: For compliance, do you have an ISO certificate?
[18:22] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II; ISO is in roadmap — will include timeline in the doc.
[18:33] Diego Martins: Could you run the benchmark with top_k variations so we can see P50/P95 tradeoffs?
[18:38] Liam Patel: Sure — I'll run quick runs: top_k 10,20,50.
[18:46] [typing; ~30s pause]
[19:15] Liam Patel: Results: top_k=10 end-to-end median 88ms p95 165ms; top_k=20 median 102ms p95 190ms; top_k=50 median 140ms p95 330ms. Costs scaled roughly linearly with candidate token volume.
[19:42] Anika Rao: That helps. For production we'll likely start with top_k=20 and tune.
[19:48] Maya Chen: Makes sense. We'll suggest pilot with top_k=20 and a light reranker.
[19:55] Tom Higgins: Anything else on storage sizing?
[19:59] Liam Patel: We'll calculate storage and I/O costs in TCO; for millions of docs we recommend shard sizing and dedupe strategies.
[20:10] [brief side conversation about account set-up]
[20:35] Diego Martins: Regarding evals, can Optimize run counterfactuals on quantization?
[20:40] Liam Patel: Yes — it can run quantized evals and show delta on NDCG. Usually int8 has minimal drop for rerankers.
[20:52] Anika Rao: How long to spin up a pilot?
[20:55] Maya Chen: We can start a hosted pilot within 48 hours after an NDA + access confirmation.
[21:02] Tom Higgins: Who will own the pilot on your side?
[21:06] Maya Chen: I'll own the pilot program and Liam will run technical orchestration.
[21:11] Anika Rao: On our side Diego & Tom will run ML + infra.
[21:16] [murmur of agreement]
[21:20] Liam Patel: Quick note on failure modes — we surfaced fallback to a simpler lexical ranker when the model times out. We can set automatic fallback policies in the Console.
[21:34] Diego Martins: Good. One last question — do you publish latency SLO numbers for hosted endpoints?
[21:39] Maya Chen: We publish typical latencies in our model catalog and can share per-model performance profiles. Hosted SLA is part of our Dedicated offering.
[21:51] Anika Rao: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[21:55] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) We'll send pricing TCO spreadsheet and security pack (Maya) 2) Liam will send reranker benchmark config and sample code (Liam) 3) Diego will send traffic profile and labeled eval set (Diego) 4) Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2025-10-13 — proposed by Maya.
[22:24] Tom Higgins: Sounds good. Any blockers for pilot?
[22:27] Anika Rao: Need internal approval for budget; we'll confirm by 2025-10-08.
[22:33] Maya Chen: Noted.
[22:36] [end of main Q&A — small chatter]
[23:00] Liam Patel: I'll drop links in the follow-up: Console runbook, SDK snippets, rerank benchmark gist, and our security whitepaper.
[23:12] Diego Martins: Thanks.
[23:15] Anika Rao: Thank you, very helpful demo.
[23:18] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlap occasionally mis-attributed, some technical acronyms may be spelled odd in auto transcript (e.g., H-N-S-W as HNSW vs H N S W).

End of meeting.
